name: Make homemade tortillas
blurb: Three ingredients, ten minutes, and a result so much better than shop-bought that it changes what you cook. Corn and flour versions teach different things.
gear: Masa harina for corn, or plain flour and fat for flour tortillas
A tortilla press, or a heavy pan and a plastic bag
A dry cast-iron skillet or comal
steps: For corn: mix masa harina with warm water and a little salt to a play-dough consistency that does not crack at the edges when pressed.
Rest the dough 20 minutes so the masa fully hydrates.
Press between two sheets of plastic to about 2 mm, then peel carefully.
Cook on a dry, hot pan: about 30 seconds, flip, a minute, flip again — the third flip is when it puffs.
Keep them wrapped in a clean towel to steam and soften.
For flour tortillas, cut fat into flour, add hot water, rest the dough, then roll thin and cook the same way.
tips: Cracked edges when pressing means the dough is too dry. Add water a teaspoon at a time.
The puff on the third flip is the sign of a well-hydrated, well-cooked tortilla.
Masa harina is not cornflour or polenta. It must be nixtamalised.
proof: A dozen soft, pliable tortillas that puff on the pan and stay foldable when cool.
